bullets.title: AI 'Pacing' Debate: Semis/Hardware sell-off seen as overreaction; capex orders intact
bullets.body: Anthropic CEO Amodei's call to slow frontier model development triggered a sharp intraday move: AMD -6.3%, MRVL -9.0%, ORCL -5.6%, AVGO -4.1%, NVDA -4.1%, while MSFT +0.3%, GOOGL +1.4%, META +2.1%. Multiple desks (Klein, DADCO, MS) argue the sell-off is an overreaction analogous to Feb 2026's Cetrini scare — Anthropic's own custom ASIC orders from AVGO signal continued heavy investment, and multi-year compute buildouts cannot be paused without ceding market share. Trump publicly opposed slowdown calls, signaling light-touch regulation ahead.

bullets.title: CRWD: +14-15% surge to 52-week high on AI-driven cybersecurity flight-to-quality
bullets.body: CrowdStrike hit a new 52-week high at ~$238, up ~15%, on 141-217% above-average volume as the AI safety debate paradoxically boosted cybersecurity spending expectations. Citi noted CRWD's Falcon Guardian (AIDR) directly addresses autonomous AI agent security; OpenAI and Anthropic are CRWD customers. Consensus frames CRWD, PANW, and OKTA as flight-to-quality beneficiaries of AI-driven attack surface expansion.

bullets.title: META: Most attractive Mag-7 valuation at ~17.5x; Muse ranked #5 in App Store
bullets.body: Citi flags META trading at ~17.5x, a ~2.5x discount to its 10-year average, with the most EPS upside potential vs. GOOGL and AMZN. MS notes Muse peaked at #2 in the App Store and settled at #5, competing against football season gambling apps, but the long-term value case is strong given 3.6B users, ads, commerce, and infrastructure. Zuckerberg's strategy centers on owning the tech layer/interface rather than needing the best frontier model.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone Duo seen as most consequential product since Apple Watch; 7M units in 2H26 at $1,999
bullets.body: MS Asia keeps 3Q26 iPhone builds at 54M (+4% q/q) and introduces 4Q26 at 73M (+35% q/q); 7M Duo builds expected in 2H26 at $1,999 starting price, better than $2,300+ feared. C2 modem confirmed in Duo and iPhone 18 Pro. MS calls foldables a 50%+ share of global smartphones within a decade vs. 2% today, framing Duo as an extreme scarcity event with secondary market markups by early 2027.

bullets.title: ORCL: Ellison cancels $7.5B stock sale; new layoff round launched today
bullets.body: Citi flagged that Oracle CEO Larry Ellison canceled a planned $7.5B stock sale and the company launched a new round of layoffs expected today. ORCL was down ~5.6% on AI slowdown concerns. The stock sale cancellation could be read as Ellison retaining confidence in the stock at current levels.

bullets.title: APP: eCommerce store growth accelerating to 2.7% weekly; 3Q guidance reaffirmed
bullets.body: Citi's weekly tracker shows AppLovin Ads reached 12,467 global eCommerce clients as of Sept 14, up 3.7% WoW, with international stores growing 7.1% vs. US 1.9%. Average weekly growth over the last five weeks accelerated to ~2.7% vs. 1.8% 3Q26 average, implying ~11.6K avg store count for 3Q. Citi notes APP is well-positioned to meet/exceed its 3Q26 guidance of 7-8% sequential growth.

bullets.title: RBLX: CCUs flat sequentially at 16.1M; bookings tracking above guidance at $1.67B
bullets.body: Citi's Week 37 RoMonitor shows average peak CCUs of 16.1M, down 16% YoY but flat sequentially, consistent with bookings of $1.67B, above the high-end of company guidance ($1.65B) and VA consensus ($1.61B). 'Steal an Egg' emerged as a standout experience. Management struck a conciliatory tone on safety at RDC 2026 with new AI game-creation tools showing strong innovation.

bullets.title: CHTR: Wolfe downgrades to Underperform, PT $118; Cox acquisition doesn't fix deteriorating broadband
bullets.body: Wolfe cuts CHTR to Underperform with a $118 PT, arguing DSL conversions dry up in 2027-28, Starlink V3 carries ~22x V2 downlink capacity with sharply falling unit costs, and fiber operators are cutting prices. The Cox acquisition adds ~33M residential subscribers but Cox's base is declining >3x faster than Charter core; even with $1B+ in cost synergies, combined EBITDA is projected to decline post-close. Comcast kept at Peer Perform; NBCU spinout valued at ~$31/share provides support.

bullets.title: RH: Q2 beat tariff-driven; Q3 guidance 400bps light; analyst PT cuts dominate
bullets.body: RH's Q2 EPS beat was largely driven by ~$55M in tariff refunds (+600bps gross margin); ex-refunds, core FY26 margins are down ~140bps. Q3 revenue guidance of 5-6% was ~400bps below consensus with EBITDA margin 590bps light. TD Cowen cut PT to $190 (from $220), Wells Fargo to $175 (from $225), Goldman raised to $164 (from $155). Average PT fell 6.7% to $160.69; sell-side is 33% buy, 57% hold. RH Estates and early London demand (~$7M in 8 weeks) are the bull case for Q4's guided 16-21% growth.

bullets.title: PLTR: DADCO upgrades to Buy on AI-driven cybersecurity/code-hardening opportunity
bullets.body: DADCO upgraded Palantir to Buy, highlighting PLTR's software assurance and code-hardening initiatives as a direct beneficiary of AI-enabled cyberattacks exploiting software vulnerabilities. MSFT, AMZN, and GOOGL also cited as platform winners given broad enterprise reach to embed security tooling.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS reiterates Buy/$275 PT (Street High); Capgemini US Federal divestiture opens share gain
bullets.body: UBS reiterates Buy on Accenture with a $275 Street-high PT (~16x 2028E EPS) as Capgemini divests its US Government business to ITC Federal. ACN Federal Services (~8% of revenue) has grown federal IT share from ~2% in FY14 to ~5% in FY24; Gen AI could contribute ~250-300bps of annual growth. FY26 faces ~1% revenue headwind from Federal that should anniversary in FY27.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Week 1 and Indiana/Iowa August data both negative for sportsbooks
bullets.body: NFL Week 1 industry hold estimated at 8-10%, below average, as 73% of favorites won, TD scoring surged ~34% YoY, and public won ~67% on moneylines. Separately, Indiana August sports betting GGR fell 19% YoY on a 9.5% hold rate (-330bps) for DKNG with handle down 4%; Iowa statewide casino GGR declined 13.1% YoY. FanDuel also down 26% in Indiana. Hold rate compression is the consistent theme across all operators.

bullets.title: NVDA: In talks to invest $10B as anchor in Anthropic IPO at ~$2T valuation
bullets.body: Per Axios/StreetAccount, NVDA is in discussions to invest $10B as an anchor investor in Anthropic's anticipated IPO, which could raise up to $100B at a ~$2T valuation. Anthropic achieved positive adjusted operating income for a second-straight quarter with >80% gross margins and expects to list on Nasdaq with an IPO prospectus expected in late September.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: DOJ expanding antitrust probe into Fox's acquisition of Roku
bullets.body: StreetAccount flagged that the Justice Department is expanding its probe into Fox's acquisition of Roku and is expected to submit a Second Request. Citizens separately initiated FOXA at Market Outperform with a $95 TP, calling out FOXA's live sports focus and the Roku deal as adding digital distribution/advertising. PSKY (Paramount Skydance) initiated at Outperform with $14 TP on planned WBD acquisition.

bullets.title: PSKY/CMCSA: SkyShowtime JV exploring strategic options including potential shutdown
bullets.body: Hollywood Reporter flagged that Paramount Skydance and Comcast are reviewing strategic options for SkyShowtime, their European streaming JV, including a potential shutdown. No decisions have been made. PSKY was up $0.40 to $11.00 at time of alert.

bullets.title: CLS: Down 7.3% on management changes
bullets.body: Celestica (CLS) fell 7.3% in Canadian trading to C$445.41 on management changes announced today. No further detail on the nature of the changes was provided in the item.

bullets.title: SHOP: Down 11.1% last week, -19.3% YTD in TSX composite
bullets.body: Shopify was among the top weekly losers in the S&P TSX Composite for the week ending Sept 11, declining 11.1% and now down 19.3% year-to-date. No specific catalyst was cited beyond broader tech/growth pressure.

bullets.title: MU: Hedgeye calls Micron the best semiconductor short; memory fundamentally bearish
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough flagged Micron (MU) as the 'best semiconductor short,' citing fundamentally bearish memory dynamics. The call comes alongside a broader bearish pivot on semis, QQQ, and SPY, with the KOSPI down 27% from its June 2026 AI bubble peak cited as a leading indicator.

bullets.title: CRDO: Jefferies BUY/$270 PT; NDR with CEO/CFO on Sept 29 in NYC
bullets.body: Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis maintains a Buy rating on Credo Semiconductor with a $270 price target. An NDR with CEO Bill Brennan and CFO Dan Fleming is scheduled for September 29 in New York. CRDO's high-speed copper/optical interconnect products serve AI data infrastructure with power delivery up to 1.6T; Klein separately noted LITE holds ~33% of EML market and AVGO/LITE are leading in UHP CW laser supply.

bullets.title: IONQ: Jefferies BUY/$80 PT; CFO NDR in NYC on Nov 9
bullets.body: Jefferies analyst Kevin Garrigan maintains a Buy rating on IonQ with an $80 price target. CFO Inder Singh is hosting investor meetings in New York on November 9. IonQ builds trapped-ion quantum computing systems accessible via AWS Braket, Microsoft Azure Quantum, and Google Cloud.
